root_cause.text: The LiquidIO PF `setup_nic_devices()` error-cleanup path had an off-by-one bug in its index handling, so the loop skipped the currently failing NIC slot and failed to destroy one allocated `nic_device`, causing a memory leak in `drivers/net/ethernet/cavium/liquidio/lio_main.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `while (i--)` to `do { ... } while (i--);` and adds `i--;` before jumping to `setup_nic_dev_free` on `devlink` allocation failure, with the commit message explicitly stating that the cleanup loop “skip[ped] the failing index i, causing a memory leak.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the NIC device setup error path by correcting the device index after a failed devlink allocation.
intent_record.what: In the error path after a failed `devlink` allocation in `setup_nic_devices()`, the code now decrements `i` before jumping to `setup_nic_dev_free`.
intent_record.how: This adjusts the loop/index state when `devlink` allocation fails, so cleanup or retry logic that uses `i` does not treat the failed device as successfully processed. It prevents an off-by-one accounting error during teardown after allocation failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix NIC device failure cleanup to ensure the failed interface index is destroyed during teardown.
intent_record.what: The cleanup loop in `setup_nic_devices()` was changed from a `while (i--)` loop to a `do { ... } while (i--);` loop, with the loop body remaining the same: it logs the failure for `i` and calls `liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the teardown behavior so the cleanup code executes at least once when control reaches `setup_nic_dev_free`, ensuring the current `i` index is also handled during failure cleanup instead of potentially skipping the first cleanup iteration.

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the relevant cleanup logic is fully shown in `setup_nic_devices()`. The error path ends at `setup_nic_dev_fail:` with `while (i--) { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }`. Because `i` is decremented in the loop condition, the cleanup starts at `i-1` and skips the currently failing index `i`, which matches the described off-by-one bug in error cleanup. The snippet also shows that one `netdev`/`nic_device` was allocated per loop iteration via `netdev = alloc_etherdev_mq(...)` and stored in `props->netdev = netdev;`, so skipping the failing slot would leave one allocated device undisposed, causing a leak. There is no compensating fix here such as destroying `i` before decrementing or looping from `i` down to 0 inclusive, so `is_fixed` is false.
